channel.title: The Grant Desk - Artist Residencies, US, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Artist Residencies, US, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: Mabou Mines SUITE/space Residency 2027-2029 (NYC early-career interdisciplinary performance, two USD 4,000 stipends) (closes 22 Nov)
item.description:
Mabou Mines
Deadline: 22 Nov 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: Two USD 4,000 stipends (dependent on funding), plus 100 hours of rehearsal space and technical support. No application fee.

SUITE/space is Mabou Mines' two-year performance residency for early-career interdisciplinary artists in New York whose practices come from lived experiences at the margins. WHO: NYC-based early-career interdisciplinary performance artists.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: WVU Libraries Artist in Residence 2027: Common Threads, Industry, Labor and Community (USD 1,000 honorarium) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
West Virginia University Libraries
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: USD 1,000 honorarium plus up to USD 1,000 materials and up to USD 3,000 travel and lodging. No application fee.

An archive-based residency in which the artist works with WVU Libraries' union records and oral histories on industry, labor and community. Digital media is eligible. ELIGIBILITY: US- and Canada-based artists aged 18 and over.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Kent Cultural Alliance SFW Residency, Spring 2027 "SERVICE": six-week live-in residency in Chestertown, Maryland (USD 7,500 stipend) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Kent Cultural Alliance
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 17:00 EST
Award: USD 7,500 stipend for the six-week session, travel reimbursed up to USD 1,000, studio and gallery expenses reimbursed up to USD 1,500, and on-site housing with a private en-suite bedroom. No application fee.

A community-engaged residency on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Three artists live and work for six weeks in the Raimond Cultural Center, a restored historic house, around the theme SERVICE, working with local partners For All Seasons, the Kent County Food Pantry and Sumner Hall.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Glen Foerd Artist in Residence 2027: year-long residency for a Philadelphia performance artist or collective (USD 3,000 stipend) (closes 6 Dec)
item.description:
Glen Foerd
Deadline: 6 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 3,000 stipend for materials, time and costs, paid in three instalments. USD 10 application fee, waived on request.

Glen Foerd, a riverside historic estate in Philadelphia, selects one Philadelphia-based performance artist or collective for its 2027 residency. Performance is read broadly: music, theatre, film and social practice all count.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Petrides Residency for a Greek Artist in NY (NYFA x ISCP): funded three-month Brooklyn studio residency (USD 9,000 stipend) (closes 8 Dec)
item.description:
New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA) with sculptor George Petrides and the International Studio & Curatorial Program (ISCP)
Deadline: 8 Dec 2026, 17:00 EST
Award: Fully funded three-month residency with a private studio, a USD 9,000 stipend, a USD 1,000 travel payment and up to USD 300 for professional development. Housing is not arranged by ISCP. No application fee stated.

NYFA, sculptor George Petrides and the International Studio & Curatorial Program (ISCP) offer one Greek artist a fully funded three-month studio residency in Brooklyn.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: University of Notre Dame: Love Ethic Social Innovator Fellowships 2028 (residency plus USD 15,000 and up to USD 50,000 project funding) (closes 11 Dec)
item.description:
University of Notre Dame, Institute for Ethics and the Common Good
Deadline: 11 Dec 2026
Award: Stipend for housing during the residency plus relocation support; USD 15,000 to the fellow's organisation to offset the four-week sabbatical; up to USD 50,000 in subgrant funding after the residency to pilot the proposed project; travel to all programme gatherings covered. No application fee.

Up to six short-term fellowships for practitioners outside academia (nonprofit leaders, community organisers, social workers, faith leaders, entrepreneurs, public-sector professionals) who want time and space to design a new initiative grounded in love-based ethics.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Craigardan Trillium Fellowship 2027 (residency for artists, activists and scholars of color, USD 4,600 + USD 500 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Craigardan
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: USD 4,600 fellowship toward a minimum two-week residency (covers the residency fee), plus a USD 500 honorarium. Travel, materials and personal expenses are not covered. USD 25 application fee (waivers available on request).

The Trillium Fellowship supports artists, activists and scholars of color working in any discipline who would benefit from the time and space to pursue their work or find creative retreat at Craigardan, a residency and farm in the Adirondacks.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: EFA SHIFT x Momus Residency 2027: six-month programme for New York artists who write and writers who make art (USD 2,000 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts (EFA Studios) with Momus
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: Artist honorarium of USD 2,000, within a six-month residency at EFA Studios with monthly critical seminars and mentoring. No application fee stated.

A new iteration of EFA's SHIFT Residency, run with the art criticism platform Momus and focused on where artistic practice meets critical writing.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: SPACES: Echo Artist Residency (Cleveland, paired residency with honorarium and production budget) (closes 10 Feb 2027)
item.description:
SPACES
Deadline: 10 Feb 2027
Award: Artist honorarium and production budget plus lodging in the gallery. SPACES does not publish figures; the Alliance of Artists Communities listing gives a USD 2,000 artist stipend plus USD 500 for travel and materials. No application fee.

Echo is a paired residency at SPACES in Cleveland: each season it selects one Northeast Ohio artist (Cuyahoga and contiguous counties) and one artist from outside the region as a peer cohort, preferring complementary or intersecting themes, though collaboration is not required.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Kala Art Institute: Media Arts Fellowship 2027-28 (Berkeley; USD 3,000 stipend) (closes 1 Mar 2027)
item.description:
Kala Art Institute
Deadline: 1 Mar 2027
Award: USD 3,000 stipend plus facility access.

Kala's long-running Media Arts Fellowship supports four artists working in film and video, sound, animation, performance cinema and media installation. ELIGIBILITY: local, national and international artists not enrolled in a degree programme.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest: Artist in Residence 2027 (Kentucky, USD 2,500 stipend) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest (Arts in Nature programme)
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: USD 2,500 stipend, plus a furnished one-bedroom cabin (kitchen, bath, Wi-Fi), a studio near a 32-acre lake, staff support, and free or discounted classes and events. No application fee stated.

Annual residency in which artists live at Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest and create site-specific work inspired by total immersion in the natural environment. WHO: visual and mixed-media artists, including those working with sound and with performance that incorporates visual elements.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellowships 2027-28 (University of Michigan) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Wallace House Center for Journalists, University of Michigan
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 85,000 stipend plus USD 5,000 relocation (figures from secondary listings; confirm on the official site).

An academic-year fellowship for mid-career journalists to pursue a study project at the University of Michigan, with seminars and programming at Wallace House. DEADLINES: international applicants 1 December 2026, 11:59 pm ET; US applicants 1 February 2027. No application fee stated.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston: Core Residency Program 2027-29 (USD 100,000 over 23 months, artists and critical writers) (closes 8 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Core Residency Program, Glassell School of Art, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (MFAH)
Deadline: 8 Jan 2027
Award: USD 100,000 (USD 50,000 per year) plus a health and wellness stipend, private studio, and free or discounted Glassell School classes. Application fee USD 12.

Two-year residency for exceptional, highly motivated emerging artists and critical writers committed to developing a sustainable practice.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Knight Science Journalism Academic-Year Fellowship 2027-28 (MIT) (closes 9 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT
Deadline: 9 Jan 2027
Award: USD 87,500 stipend over 9.5 months, plus USD 5,000 for travel and housing, health insurance and a childcare subsidy. No application fee.

An academic-year fellowship at MIT for journalists covering science, health, technology or the environment, with seminars, MIT and Harvard courses and a self-directed study project.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: School for Advanced Research: Native Artist Fellowships 2027 (USD 15,000 plus Santa Fe residency) (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
School for Advanced Research, Indian Arts Research Center
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027
Award: USD 15,000 stipend plus housing, studio space, a supplies allowance and travel. No application fee stated.

The Indian Arts Research Center at the School for Advanced Research offers three residential fellowships for Native American artists: the Eric and Barbara Dobkin Fellowship for Native women artists working in any media (including digital art and film/video), the Ronald and Susan Dubin Fellowship...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Generator Residency (Kairos x Constellation, Winter 2027)
item.description: Kairos and Constellation · deadline 01 Nov 2026 · USD 8,500 per month stipend (some Embedded track residents employed at a roughly equivalent salary), plus travel to and from Berkeley. No application fee.

item.title: Adirondack Experience (ADKX) Artist-in-Residence 2027
item.description: Adirondack Experience, The Museum on Blue Mountain Lake (ADKX) · deadline 11 Dec 2026 · USD 5,000 stipend per one-month residency, plus USD 500 travel allowance, USD 250 Art Lab materials allowance, and free on-site housing with utilities, wi-fi and laundry included.
